title: Reserved-pool thin provisioning causes intermittent tenant burst denials — triage & mitigation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Customer escalation from a large fintech tenant reporting repeated brief 429/POOL_CAPACITY errors during predictable end-of-day batch windows. Investigation shows reserved pool "thin provisioning" (headroom delta between optimistic reservation and actual allocatable slots) combined with AZ skew and heterogeneous GPU capacity accounting. This caused burst allocations to be denied even though overall cluster utilization was below absolute capacity. Problem impacts Dedicated and Private deployments where reserved pools are used for predictable throughput.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a reserved pool with mixed GPU types (A100+H100) and enable tenant burst credits
2) Run parallel warmup traffic from two tenants with differing seq-length profiles to populate KV cache unevenly
3) Simulate end-of-day microburst (80% of tenant requests in 2m window) while autoscaler is in grace period
4) Observe allocation failures and 429s from allocator/placement service despite free GPU memory on some nodes
5) Correlate with headroom telemetry and per-AZ reservation counters to confirm thin provision mismatch.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:15 — Support ticket from customer: repeated 429s across 6x 1m windows. SLA breach reported.
Telemetry: allocator.free_slots shows 0 in AZ-us-west-2b while AZ-us-west-2c shows free_slots > 20; redis-burnt-reservations metric incrementing.

Root cause hypothesis: our reservation step assumes homogeneous slot equivalence across GPU types; placement uses a conservative headroom delta for H100 nodes leading to fragmentation where small-sequence requests get packed inefficiently and burst tokens are rejected when cached KV and model shards increase memory pressure.

Rediscovery: a recent change (runtime-1.21) adjusted warmup sample weighting; combined with a stale headroom calculation in the reserve allocator, it effectively undercounted usable slots for heterogeneous pools.
Customer reproduces reliably during scheduled heavy traffic windows; non-urgent traffic unaffected.
root_cause_summary: Mismatch between reserved-slot counting and actual allocatable capacity when GPUs of different memory/compute profiles are present, exacerbated by autoscaler grace-periods and uneven KV cache warming. The reserve allocator treated GPU slots as fungible and applied a safety delta tuned for homogeneous clusters; with heterogeneous hardware the delta over-constrained certain AZs leading to silent capacity thinness.
remediation_actions: Immediate (hotfix) — Lift conservative safety delta for mixed-GPU reserved pools in allocator to allow opportunistic placement during verified low-memory pressure windows (PR #7891).
Short term — Add per-GPU-type usable_slot_estimate and adjust reservation algorithm to sum usable capacity across types rather than counting uniform slots.
Medium term — Enhance warmup/kv-cache signals to report expected working set per-tenant so autoscaler can account for cache memory when computing headroom.
Customer communication — Provide mitigation timeline and enable temporary increased burst_budget for affected tenant until patch deploys.
rollback_plan: If hotfix causes allocation regressions, revert PR #7891 and switch target tenant to a temporary dedicated coldpool with explicit headroom to avoid regressed allocations.
Notify SRE on revert and run increased telemetry sampling for 30m post-revert.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge hotfix branch and run integration tests across heterogeneous-sim cluster (2 hours)
2) Canary deploy to staging reserved-pool region and run customer-like microburst load tests (1 hour)
3) Deploy to us-west-2 with 10% traffic shadow rollout for first 30 minutes, then 100% after validation
4) Coordinate with Support to lift tenant burst_manual_override after 100% roll completes and validate 24h of stability.
verification_criteria: Zero 429/POOL_CAPACITY errors for the affected tenant during two consecutive scheduled end-of-day windows
Allocator headroom drift under 3% vs predicted capacity across AZs during microburst tests
No increase in tail latency (p95/p99 token time) attributable to placement changes.
